Abdus Samad Khan ------ Appellant

full_judgment:
Md Tafazzul Islam J: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 28-10-1998 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 613 of 1991. 

 2. The appellant instituted Title Suit No. 153 of 1982 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) 1st Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract. The above Court having found that the summons of the above suit were duly served upon both the Government and the respondent No. 1 on 19-5-1982 and 17-7-1982 respectively, posted the above suit for hearing but the hearing of the suit was adjourned on 19-8-1982, 21-9-1982 and 22-11-1982 and it was ultimately taken up for hearing on 23-1-1983 and decreed ex parte on 15-2-1983. Then on depositing the balance consideration money on 6-9-1983 the appellant filed Execution Case No.30 of 1983. Subsequently the above execution case, being transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Gazipur, was re-numbered as Execution Case No. 13 of 1985 and then sale deed was executed and registered on 13-5-1985 through Court. The respondent No. 1 then filed miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1988 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Dhaka on 9-1-1988 for restoration of the above Title Suit No. 153 of 1982 to its original file and number on setting aside the ex parte decree dated 15-2-1983 on the ground that he never entered into any contract with the appellant for sale of the suit land and he had no knowledge of the suit and that he filed the miscellaneous case within time from the date of his knowledge. The said case, on transfer to Gazipur, was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 1988. The appellant filed written objection in the above case totally denying the statements made by the respondent No. 1 in the above miscellaneous case. The learned Subordinate Judge by judgment and order dated 30-5-1991 dismissed the miscellaneous case holding that the same is barred by limitation. Then the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment, allowed the appeal upon setting aside the judgment of the trial Court and restored Title Suit No. 153 of 1982 to its file and number. 

 3. Leave was granted on the submission that the trial Court found that although it is difficult to determine whether the original defendant received the summons of the original suit or not but it has been established by evidence on record that the defendant-respondent received summons of Title Execution Case No. 30 of 1983 on 12-12-83 and, as such, he had knowledge of the original suit on 12-12-1983 but he filed the instant miscellaneous case on 9-1-1988 i.e. five years after his knowledge of the original suit and the submission that the High Court Division did not reverse the finding of the trial Court to the effect that the original defendant received the summons of Title Execution Case No. 30 of 1983 on 12-12-1983 and the High Court Division also erroneously ignoring this factum of knowledge of the original defendant, and relying solely upon the service of summons of the original suit and on other irrelevant considerations, allowed the appeal without meeting the finding of the trial Court to the effect that the miscellaneous case is barred by limitation on the ground of not filing the case within 30 days from the date of the knowledge of the original defendants on 12-12-1983. 

 5. As it appears admittedly the summons of Title Execution Case No. 30 of 1983 were served upon the respondent No. 1 on 12-12-1983 and the same amply proves the date of knowledge of the respondent No. 1 of the original Title Suit No. 153 of 1982 on 12-12-1983 but he filed the instant Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1988 on 9-1-88 i.e. long 5 years after the date of his knowledge of the original suit and the High Court Division erroneously ignored this factum of knowledge of the respondent No. 1 of the original suit and relying on the absence of proof of service of summons of the original suit upon the appellant and other irrelevant considerations allowed the appeal. It also appears that the High Court Division did not meet the reasoning’s of the trial Court and also did not consider that the miscellaneous case is barred by limitation on the ground of not filing the miscellaneous case within 30 days from date of the knowledge of original defendant i.e. on 12-12-1983. It further appears that the appellant though sufficiently established about the service of summons of the execution case upon the respondent No. 1, the High Court Division, without considering the provision of Article 164 of the Limitation Act, allowed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 613 of 1991 setting aside the ex-parte decree. So the judgment and order of the High Court Division cannot be sustained. 

 6. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the judgment and order dated 28-10-1998 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 613 of 1991 is set aside.
